title: Open a bottle with a detented safety loop and rocker latch
instruction: Open the bottle and keep it upright on the table.
context: Opening a reusable spill-resistant bottle requires stabilizing a free object while manipulating two independent mechanical restraints. This tests everyday assistive manipulation rather than unscrewing a cap or lifting an unconstrained lid.
setup: One empty grey steel-bodied bottle, 72 mm body diameter and approximately 282 mm closed height, with a dark polymer spring-opening lid, spring-return rocker hook and a polymer U-shaped safety loop (30 mm crown centreline diameter, 6 mm section diameter). Body mass 350 g, lid 25 g, rocker 7 g, loop 6 g. It stands at world XY=(0,0), base Z=0.8005 m, with both restraints engaged and the button facing -Y. A rigid rectangular worktable is 1.44 x 1.64 x 0.08 m with top Z=0.80 m; a floor plane is at Z=0. Two Panda arms with custom parallel grippers are mounted at (-0.40,-0.30,0.80) m and (0.48,0.27,0.80) m, the latter rotated 180 degrees about Z. Grippers have 8 x 8 x 24 mm distal pads, 0-90 mm jaw gap, aluminium carriers and rubber-like friction pads. Parked tool targets are (-0.12,-0.18,1.12) m and (0.13,0.16,1.12) m, pointing down with jaws open. Materials and dimensions are engineering estimates; exact geometry, colours, initial robot configuration and contact parameters are defined by the supplied scene builders. No other task objects, fixtures, liquid or tools are present.
scoring: Evaluate at 20 Hz. The score at termination counts. Each credited condition must hold for 8 consecutive control ticks (0.4 s): 1.0 if lid angle >60 degrees from closed; otherwise 0.5 if lid >15 degrees; otherwise 0.25 if safety-loop angle >=150 degrees from raised; otherwise 0. A single sampled bottle-axis dot world-up <=0.90 (tilt >=25.842 degrees), bottle-base origin Z<0.79 m, any numerical warning/nonfinite state, or sampled wrist force >100 N for 4 consecutive ticks permanently invalidates the trial and overrides all credit with 0. Full score or an invalid trial ends the episode; timeout receives the current partial score. Robot contact alone must operate the mechanism; bottle joint actuation, pose edits, object destruction and geometry edits are outside the allowed action interface.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 simulated seconds at 20 Hz). Physics integration is 0.00005 s per substep.
reset_notes: Recreate the deterministic native scene, restore the prescribed robot home joints and open jaws, solve for the parked tool targets, and settle for 10 unscored control ticks (0.5 s). Clear scorer history, force baseline and time. Seed 42 labels the fixed layout; no scene randomization. No consumables.
fidelity: Approximate contact-driven MuJoCo 3.3.7 model. Both lid restraints use explicit hook/slot/loop contact; the bottle is free, with no welds, equality latches, runtime contact switching or object pose corrections. Only 18 robot motors are actuated. The safety-loop detent is an effective piecewise angle/velocity torque with gravity compensation, not a resolved detent spring/cam. Lid/rocker springs, dimensions, mass, friction and compliance are estimated rather than calibrated. Some rings, seals and spout surfaces are visual only; there is no fluid, seal compression, breakage or flexible plastic. Rigid contacts and force thresholds do not establish real-hardware safety or measured force fidelity.
scores: Dream-1 run: not run; scripted demo: 1.0 (714 control steps, 35.7 simulated seconds).
